name: Docker

modules.title: Docker Foundations
modules.description: Understand what Docker solves and how its main parts work together.
modules.challenge: Explain the path from typing docker run to a running isolated process.

modules.title: Install & Configure
modules.description: Set up Docker Desktop or Engine and verify the environment before building.
modules.challenge: Install Docker for your operating system, run hello-world, and inspect the active context.

modules.title: Container Lifecycle
modules.description: Create, run, inspect, enter, stop, and remove containers confidently.
modules.challenge: Run an Nginx container, inspect it, execute a command inside it, then stop and remove it.

modules.title: Images & Layers
modules.description: Read image names, layers, tags, and immutable digests without guesswork.
modules.challenge: Pull an image by tag, inspect its digest and history, retag it, then remove the extra tag.

modules.title: Dockerfile Essentials
modules.description: Turn repeatable build instructions into a clear, maintainable image recipe.
modules.challenge: Write a Dockerfile for a small application that runs as a non-root user.

modules.title: BuildKit & Buildx
modules.description: Use Docker's modern builder for caching, secrets, remote builders, and multiple platforms.
modules.challenge: Create a buildx builder and produce an amd64 and arm64 image without copying secrets into a layer.

modules.title: Multi-stage & Efficient Builds
modules.description: Shrink attack surface and build time by separating compilation from runtime.
modules.challenge: Refactor a single-stage build so only the runtime artifact reaches the final image.

modules.title: Registries & Distribution
modules.description: Name, authenticate, publish, and retrieve images safely across environments.
modules.challenge: Tag a local image for a registry, authenticate securely, push it, and verify its digest.

modules.title: Storage & Persistence
modules.description: Choose the right mount for durable data, source code, or temporary memory.
modules.challenge: Persist database data in a named volume, inspect it, and describe how you would back it up.

modules.title: Container Networking
modules.description: Connect services, publish ports, and use Docker's built-in service discovery.
modules.challenge: Create a private network, connect an API and database by name, and publish only the API port.

modules.title: Docker Compose
modules.description: Define and operate a complete multi-container application in one readable YAML model.
modules.challenge: Describe a web and database stack with health-aware startup, named storage, and an internal network.

modules.title: Runtime Configuration
modules.description: Control process behavior, resources, health, and restart policy without rebuilding.
modules.challenge: Run a service with a memory limit, healthcheck, restart policy, and read-only root filesystem.

modules.title: Logs & Observability
modules.description: See what containers are doing and collect useful signals when something fails.
modules.challenge: Diagnose a restarting container using ps, logs, inspect, stats, and events in a sensible order.

modules.title: Container Security
modules.description: Reduce privilege, protect the daemon, and make safer runtime boundaries the default.
modules.challenge: Harden a container by dropping privileges, making filesystems read-only, and avoiding the Docker socket.

modules.title: Supply-chain Security
modules.description: Inspect image contents, vulnerabilities, provenance, and policy before deployment.
modules.challenge: Generate an SBOM, review critical CVEs, and explain why a signed provenance record matters.

modules.title: Developer Workflow
modules.description: Use Docker for fast, repeatable local development without hiding feedback.
modules.challenge: Design a local workflow where source changes are synced but dependencies and database data remain cached.

modules.title: CI/CD & Publishing
modules.description: Build once, test predictably, and publish immutable images through automation.
modules.challenge: Outline a pipeline that tests, builds, scans, and pushes a commit-tagged multi-platform image.

modules.title: Production & Swarm
modules.description: Operate services across nodes with controlled rollout, scale, configuration, and recovery.
modules.challenge: Deploy a replicated service with a secret, health-aware rolling update, and safe rollback plan.

1: Containers share the host kernel and isolate processes; VMs boot a complete guest operating system.
The docker command is a client that sends API requests to a Docker daemon.
dockerd builds images, creates networks and volumes, and manages container lifecycle.
Images are templates; containers are runnable instances; networks and volumes connect and persist them.

docker image ls
docker container ls
A registry stores and distributes tagged or digest-addressed images.
Namespaces isolate what a process can see; cgroups limit and account for resources it can use.
OCI defines interoperable image/runtime standards while containerd handles lower-level container lifecycle for Docker.
2: Desktop bundles the Engine, CLI, Compose, BuildKit, and a graphical dashboard for local development.
Engine is the daemon-led container runtime commonly installed directly on Linux servers.
The CLI exposes commands and built-in help for objects such as containers, images, and networks.
The hello-world image verifies that the client can reach the daemon and pull and run an image.
A context stores connection settings so one CLI can target local or remote Docker endpoints.

docker context ls
docker context use default
docker version shows client and server versions separately, which helps reveal API mismatches.
daemon.json controls Engine-wide settings such as logging, registries, and data location.
3: docker run creates a new container from an image, applies the requested settings, and starts the image's configured process.
docker create prepares a container without running it, while docker start launches that same prepared container later.

docker create --name job alpine echo done
docker start -a job
docker stop requests a graceful shutdown and waits for a timeout; docker kill sends a signal immediately when waiting is inappropriate.

docker stop web
docker kill web
restart cycles a container; rm deletes a stopped container and its writable layer.

docker restart web
docker rm -f web
exec starts an additional command inside an already-running container.
logs reads captured output; attach connects your terminal to the container's main process.
inspect returns configuration JSON; stats shows resource use; top lists container processes.

docker inspect web
docker stats web
docker top web
4: Each filesystem-changing build instruction creates a reusable read-only layer.
A tag is a movable human-friendly image reference, commonly used for versions.
A digest is an immutable content hash, so it identifies exactly one image manifest.
pull downloads an image; push uploads a tagged image to a registry you can access.

docker pull alpine:3.20
docker push username/myapp:1.0
history shows the commands and sizes that formed an image's layers.
A manifest list can point one tag to architecture-specific images such as amd64 and arm64.
prune removes unused image data; review disk usage before reclaiming it.

docker system df
docker image prune
5: FROM selects a base image and starts a build stage.
RUN executes a build-time command and commits its filesystem result to a layer.
COPY transfers local build-context files; ADD has extra archive and URL behavior and should be intentional.
WORKDIR sets the directory used by later instructions and by the launched process.
ENTRYPOINT defines the executable while CMD supplies default arguments or the default command.
ARG exists while building; ENV persists in the image and is available to the running container.
USER drops privileges, EXPOSE documents a port, and LABEL adds searchable metadata.
6: BuildKit is Docker's modern build backend and can skip unused work and run independent stages in parallel.
The context is the file set a build may read; keep it small to make transfers and cache checks faster.
.dockerignore excludes files such as Git history, dependencies, and secrets from the build context.
A cache mount reuses package-manager data without placing that cache in the final image layer.
A secret mount exposes sensitive data only to one build step and does not bake it into the image.
An SSH mount forwards an agent temporarily so a build can fetch private source without copying a key.
buildx manages advanced builders and can publish one tag containing multiple architecture variants.
7: Multiple FROM instructions create stages so build tools can stay out of the final runtime image.

FROM golang:1.24 AS build
RUN go build -o /out/app .
FROM gcr.io/distroless/base
COPY --from=build /out/app /app
AS gives a stage a stable name that COPY --from can reference even if stages are reordered.
--target stops at a named stage, which is useful for testing or debugging intermediate output.
Place stable dependency steps before frequently changing source so more layers remain reusable.

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
A version tag or digest reduces surprise changes; a digest gives exact reproducibility.
A focused runtime base contains fewer packages, downloads faster, and exposes fewer components.
A non-root runtime executes the application as an unprivileged user, reducing what a compromised container process can change or access.
8: A repository groups versions of an image under a registry namespace and name.
A complete reference can include registry host, namespace, repository, tag, and digest.
login stores or delegates registry credentials so pull and push can authenticate.
Registry access tokens are limited credentials for pull or push operations and are safer for automation than exposing a user's main password.
A private registry limits who may discover, pull, or push organization images.
A credential helper keeps registry secrets in an operating-system keychain instead of plain config.
A mirror caches upstream content closer to builders and can reduce latency or rate-limit pressure.
9: Changes not mounted elsewhere live in the container's disposable writable layer.
Docker-managed volumes persist independently of a container and are the usual choice for application data.

docker volume create pgdata
docker run -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17
A bind mount exposes an exact host path, which is useful for source code but tightly couples host layout.
A tmpfs keeps temporary data in host memory and does not persist it to the container layer.
--mount names source, target, type, and options explicitly and is easier to review than short syntax.
A helper container can archive the mounted volume without installing backup tools in the application image.
docker run --rm -v data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine tar czf /backup/data.tgz /data
Multiple containers can mount the same data; use read-only mode for consumers that must not modify it.
10: A bridge is the standard single-host network; user-defined bridges add automatic DNS by container name.
-p maps a host address and port to a container port; EXPOSE alone does not publish it.
On a user-defined network, containers resolve one another by name or network alias.
Host mode removes network namespace isolation and lets the process use the host network directly.
None leaves a container with loopback only, useful when it needs no network access.
Overlay joins services across Docker hosts; macvlan gives containers addresses on a physical network.
Internal networks block external routing; IPv6 can be enabled where daemon and network configuration support it.
11: Compose represents an application as services connected by networks and persistent resources.
Each service defines how one application component is built or run.
In Compose, build specifies how to create an image from source, while image identifies what to run and optionally names the built result.
These sections declare host exposure, persistent mounts, and communication boundaries.
environment passes explicit values; env_file loads container variables from a file.
depends_on controls creation order and can wait for a dependency healthcheck, not just process start.
Profiles enable optional services; Compose Watch syncs or rebuilds as development files change.

docker compose --profile debug up
docker compose watch
12: -e supplies runtime configuration and overrides image ENV values without changing the image.
Resource flags stop one container from consuming unbounded host CPU or memory.
A restart policy tells the daemon when to relaunch a stopped container.
A healthcheck reports whether the service is functioning, independently of whether its process still exists.
PID 1 handles signals and orphaned children specially; --init adds a small init process when needed.
Read-only mode prevents writes to the image filesystem; add explicit writable mounts for required paths.
Capabilities add or drop focused kernel privileges; sysctls tune allowed namespaced kernel parameters.
13: Containers should usually write application logs to standard streams so Docker can collect them.
A logging driver routes container output to json-file, local, journald, syslog, or another destination.
Size and file limits stop local log files from silently filling the host disk.
events streams daemon activity such as create, start, die, network, and volume actions.
stats reports live CPU, memory, network, block I/O, and process counts.
inspect exposes low-level state and Go templates can select just the value you need.
exec can inspect a running container; docker debug can add tools without permanently bloating a slim image.
14: Grant only the users, mounts, networks, and kernel capabilities the process genuinely needs.
Rootless Docker runs daemon and containers without host root privileges, reducing daemon compromise impact.
User namespace remapping maps container root to an unprivileged host identity.
The default seccomp profile blocks risky system calls while permitting common container workloads.
Linux security modules add mandatory access rules beyond ordinary Unix permissions.
Mounting docker.sock effectively grants control of the daemon and often the host; avoid it or proxy narrowly.
Provide secrets through a managed secret mechanism or temporary file, not an image layer or committed env file.
15: Scout analyzes image components and compares them with vulnerability and policy data.
A software bill of materials lists the packages and components present in an image.
CVE reports connect vulnerable packages with severity and available fixes.
Rebuilding with a patched base can remove inherited vulnerabilities even when app code is unchanged.
Provenance records how and where an image was built so consumers can verify its origin.
An SBOM attestation travels alongside the image manifest in the registry.
A CI policy can block release when images violate approved base, severity, or freshness rules.
16: A development container standardizes tools and dependencies while the editor stays connected to the workspace.
Mounting source gives immediate file changes without rebuilding every edit.
An additional Compose file can layer development-only ports, mounts, or commands onto a shared base.
Watch can sync files, restart a service, or rebuild when selected paths change.
A language-specific watcher reloads the process when mounted or synced source changes.
Disposable Compose projects make integration tests repeatable and easy to tear down.
Remote builders can share cache and powerful build capacity while the developer keeps a local CLI.
17: Separate test, build, scan, and publish steps so failures stop promotion at the right boundary.
Tag releases with a commit or version; do not depend on latest as the only production identity.
CI registry authentication uses short-lived or narrowly scoped secrets, passed through standard input so credentials do not appear in command arguments or logs.
Export and import BuildKit cache so clean runners can reuse expensive dependency layers.
A buildx push can publish architecture variants and their manifest list in one operation.
Docker's maintained actions set up Buildx, authenticate, generate metadata, and build and push.
Promote the tested digest between environments so deployment cannot drift to different bytes.
18: A swarm groups Engines into manager and worker nodes with an encrypted control plane.
A service declares desired state; the orchestrator schedules individual task containers to match it.
A stack deploys a group of services, networks, configs, and secrets from a Compose-style file.
An overlay network lets swarm services communicate across nodes and supports routing mesh ingress.
Replica counts and placement constraints control capacity and where tasks may run.
Update settings control parallelism and delay; rollback restores the previous service specification.

docker service update --image nginx:1.28 --update-parallelism 2 web
docker service rollback web
Secrets are encrypted in the swarm and mounted only into authorized tasks; configs hold non-sensitive files.

docker secret create db_password ./password.txt
docker service create --secret db_password app

Docker objects:
docker image ls
docker container ls
Docker contexts:
docker context ls
docker context use default
create and start:
docker create --name job alpine echo done
docker start -a job
stop and kill:
docker stop web
docker kill web
restart and remove:
docker restart web
docker rm -f web
inspect, stats and top:
docker inspect web
docker stats web
docker top web
Pull and push:
docker pull alpine:3.20
docker push username/myapp:1.0
Image cleanup:
docker system df
docker image prune
Multi-stage builds:
FROM golang:1.24 AS build
RUN go build -o /out/app .
FROM gcr.io/distroless/base
COPY --from=build /out/app /app
Cache ordering:
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
Named volumes:
docker volume create pgdata
docker run -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17
Volume backup and restore: docker run --rm -v data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine tar czf /backup/data.tgz /data
profiles and watch:
docker compose --profile debug up
docker compose watch
Rolling updates and rollback:
docker service update --image nginx:1.28 --update-parallelism 2 web
docker service rollback web
Swarm secrets and configs:
docker secret create db_password ./password.txt
docker service create --secret db_password app
